day_shape: 60 items: Iran advances Strait of Hormuz transit-fee and violator-restrictions regime, Trump signals broader US Treasury secondary sanctions, IDF strikes in Gaza and southern Lebanon, Houthis claim Red Sea tanker hit, heavy Government Week regime messaging.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz transit restrictions
threads.summary: Iran's Persian Gulf Waterway Management Authority warned vessels violating Iranian arrangements for Hormuz transit could face fines, detention or confiscation, while a parliamentary committee advanced a plan to charge vessels for services. Jerusalem Post cited a security analyst linking the move to US sanctions pressure; a separate opinion piece framed Hormuz as Iran's remaining leverage.

threads.label: US sanctions pressure and Iran cyber posture
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Trump posted on Truth Social that Iran is 'completely collapsing' as the US Treasury is expected to broaden secondary sanctions, and that Britain briefed energy company executives after Iran-linked hackers shut down a small UK energy facility. Iranian state-affiliated Channel 3 was reported to have released a video threatening Barron Trump and offering a $10 million bounty.

threads.label: IDF strikes in Gaza and southern Lebanon
threads.summary: The IDF said an overnight airstrike in Deir al-Balah killed Nukhba operative Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad and a second October 7 participant, and the air force struck what it called a weapons depot in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City. Jerusalem Post cited Lebanese security officials describing extensive Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon as groundwork for a broader campaign; IRIB relayed Al Jazeera reports of two Israeli strikes near Tyre.

threads.label: Houthi Red Sea tanker claim
threads.summary: Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree announced Yemeni forces struck the Saudi tanker 'Amzan' with a ballistic missile off Yanbu in the northern Red Sea, claiming a direct hit and fire on board. Defa Press and IRIB carried the claim alongside reports of Yemeni attacks on Saudi-backed positions.

threads.label: Government Week messaging and post-war framing
threads.summary: On Iran's Government Week, the IRGC, Army and senior commanders including Sepah spokesman Brigadier Mohseni, Army chief General Hatami and Admiral Siayari issued statements framing government-military 'synergy' as key to withstanding sanctions and warning against strikes on Iranian infrastructure. Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghei warned Bulgaria over refuelling aircraft, and judiciary chief Ajeei said 7.5 billion euros in foreign-exchange obligations had been recovered.

The price of diesel has reached 2.24 euros per litre and petrol prices have exceeded 2 euros per litre. In France, fuel prices have been increasing for the past two weeks and diesel prices have risen by 6 cents. Petrol prices in France have risen by 5 cents in just the past 20 days. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz is the main reason for the fuel price increase in France. It is predicted that the fuel price increase will result in increased costs for school transport services and French household expenses ahead of school reopening.

The biennial Sang-Yong exercise, which was to involve the naval infantry of both countries, was scheduled for next month. Donald Trump last week also ordered that another annual exercise with South Korea be reduced from 11 days to five days. The US president cited high military costs as the reason for this decision. The Pentagon has not yet responded to the announcement of the cancellation of the amphibious exercise. Previously, South Korea's president had called for military independence from the United States.
